Practice Principles

Safety & Trust
Therapeutic work begins with a secure relationship and clear limits.
Practical Insight
We translate insight into concrete next steps you can try between sessions.
Collaboration
You are the expert on your life; I bring structure, training, and reflection.

Tools I Use

  • Cognitive-behavioral techniques for anxiety and stress regulation.
  • Trauma-informed stabilization and grounding practices.
  • Relational work to address attachment concerns and communication patterns.
  • Solution-focused planning for life transitions and burnout recovery.

Common Concerns I Hear

"I don't need therapy — I just need advice." I keep sessions practical and aligned to your goals. Therapy is not about giving instructions but helping you decide which steps fit you.

"I'm too busy to commit." We often begin with short, focused work and build only as needed; many clients notice meaningful change with modest time investments.

Client Reflections

"Practical, direct, and warm. I left sessions with tools I used immediately." — A client in their 30s

Primary Areas of Care

I specialize in clear, ethically grounded therapy for adults navigating stress, relationships, and transitions. Below are common presentations I work with and the pragmatic focus each path offers.

What guides my work

Safety, evidence-informed practice, and a collaborative stance. I aim to make therapy accessible, predictable, and useful.

Anxiety Management — "Calm Skills"

Short-term focus on worry cycles, exposure planning, and physiological regulation.

Trauma Stabilization — "Foundations"

Safety, grounding, and stepwise processing; we move at a pace you can maintain.

Relationship Repair — "Relational Repair"

Communication patterns, boundaries, and attachment-informed interventions for couples or individuals.

Life Transitions & Career Shifts — "Transition Labs"

Practical exploration, values alignment exercises, and decision-making frameworks.

Burnout & Stress Recovery — "Reset Module"

Behavioral activation, pacing strategies, and restorative routines to rebuild energy.

Parenting & Family Strain

Psychoeducation and emotion coaching techniques for caregivers navigating difficult family dynamics.

Is this the right fit?

Not sure if therapy suits your need? A 20-minute consultation helps us identify whether short-term modules or ongoing psychotherapy is the best option for you.

Client Notes

"The Reset Module taught me a few habits that made my workweek manageable again." — client feedback

How We Collaborate — The Map & Milestones

A clear, flexible structure helps therapy feel purposeful. Below is how I typically organize early work and ongoing care.

Typical First 8 Sessions

1. Intake & Priorities
Clarify concerns, set short-term goals, and identify immediate supports.
2. Stabilization
Teach grounding and coping strategies to ensure safety and reduce overwhelm.
3. Skill Integration
Practice cognitive and behavioral tools in context of your life.
4. Review & Plan
Assess progress and decide whether to continue, shift focus, or taper support.

What I Promise in Sessions

  • Clear session agendas and agreed goals.
  • Respectful challenge balanced with compassionate listening.
  • Confidentiality and transparent limits of care.

Worries people bring

"What if it doesn't help?" We track progress intentionally. If you and I don't see change, I will discuss adjustments or referrals.

What clients notice

"I appreciated the structure — it made therapy feel efficient and safe." — anonymous client

Free Worksheet: My First 30 Days

Packages & Availability

I offer tiered care: single consultations, short modules (4–8 sessions), and ongoing psychotherapy. We'll choose a rhythm that fits your needs and schedule.
